newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE INDUSTRIALS END WEAK IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE INDUSTRIALS END WEAK IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares traded largely weaker on Monday, and local brokers said they expected the market to continue soft this week under some price-correction pressure.
"There is quite a bit of pressure building up and that should keep the shares down, but we may get a rise here and there to test whether that's the real market direction," one broker said.
"It (price-correction) is the sort of thing we have been expecting for a while, but never quite getting there," he said.
"There are no big players on the market...but many small guys are cashing out," he said of a market that has been bullish for most of the last three months.

The key 57-counter industrial share index plunged 123.48 points to 10,009.48 after falls in bluechips conglomerate Delta, which traded 50 cents down at 4,300 and hotel group Meikles, 50 cents down at 2,050.
The secondary seven-share mining index fell 5.06 points to 965.29 after nickel producer Bindura traded 10 cents lower in reasonable turnover at 800.
